title: Chapter 52
content:
"Fix your face," Kim Sun-young hissed under her breath.

Kang Seok-joo quickly bit his lip, wrestling the smug grin from the corners of his mouth.

Ever since the sniper's bullet tore through Kang Il-hyun at the podium, the man had been rushed into emergency trauma surgery, stabilized in the intensive care unit, and only transferred to the VIP wing earlier that morning.

The press had seized on the shooting like wild dogs, plastering Il-hyun’s critical condition across every headline and broadcast. The media circus had an unintended side effect: the brewing scandal over Chairman Kang’s illicit slush funds was swept entirely under the rug. Even the prosecution, wary of public backlash while a son hovered between life and death, had quietly postponed the Chairman's official summons.

Within Haewon Group's boardroom, the shockwaves were seismic. Factions had fractured overnight: the old guard pushing for Kang Tae-han to step in as legitimate heir; Kim Sun-young’s camp aggressively maneuvering to seat Seok-joo at the head of the table; and the pragmatic heavyweights who maintained that no one possessed the operational ruthlessness to steer the conglomerate like Kang Il-hyun.

As their motorcade pulled up to the medical center, Kim Sun-young smoothed her tailored suit, turning to give Seok-joo one final, venomous warning not to let his excitement show.

Seok-joo, for his part, was far too busy trading celebratory texts with his friends. The group chat was in a frenzy trying to deduce who had pulled the trigger; Il-hyun had amassed so many blood debts over the years that narrowing down the suspect list was practically impossible.

If only Jang Yi-an were still around to celebrate with me. Feeling a twinge of regret, Seok-joo had fired off a text, but the line remained dead.

The sedan drew to a halt before the main entrance, where a secretary opened the door. The private cars carrying Chairman Kang and Kang Tae-han pulled up in tandem, and the family marched into the lobby as a united front.

Hospital administrators and senior surgeons hurried over to bow, but the tension etched into their faces was impossible to miss.

Seok-joo understood why the moment they stepped onto the twentieth-floor VIP surgical wing.

Before they could take three paces toward the double doors of Il-hyun's suite, Park Tae-soo stepped into the corridor, planting his massive frame squarely across their path.

Chairman Kang stopped short, his brow furrowing with incredulous offense. "What is the meaning of this?"

"My apologies, Chairman," Tae-soo replied, his voice a flat, immovable wall. "You may not enter."

Tae-han exploded on the spot. "You arrogant piece of shit! A mere bodyguard barking orders at the Chairman? Who the hell do you think you're barring?! Has working under Il-hyun made you completely lose your goddamn mind?!"

Tae-han stepped forward with raised fists, ready to strike, while the hospital director hovered uselessly at his elbow, wringing his hands in helpless panic.

The elevator chimes rang out, and Kang Yu-jung stepped into the hallway.

Flanking her was a sharp young man in gold-rimmed glasses—a senior managing partner at one of Seoul's powerhouse law firms who handled Il-hyun's most sensitive, classified retainers.

Yu-jung closed the distance, greeting her family with a serene, practiced smile. "You're all here early. What a shame... I'm afraid visitation is strictly off-limits today."

Tae-han scowled, his tone rough and combative. "Why? The surgical team said the operation was a success."

Yu-jung slowly swept her gaze over each of their faces, letting a delicate, sorrowful sigh slip past her lips.

"He suffered catastrophic blood loss. He barely survived the table. He requires absolute, undisturbed rest—so please, come back another day."

The sniper's first round through the left thigh had grazed past the major femoral nerves without inflicting structural ruin, but the second shot through the right leg had severed the femoral artery completely. Even with immediate field tourniquets applied, the arterial hemorrhage had been massive, forcing the trauma team to spend grueling hours retrieving the retracted vascular bundle buried deep within the mangled muscle.

If Yu-jung hadn't defied Il-hyun's dismissive arrogance by placing a trauma team on standby—if she hadn't been in the hall herself—her brother would have bled out on the stage floor.

Kim Sun-young stepped forward, the sharp clack-clack of her stiletto heels echoing off the polished marble.

"Yu-jung, dear. We only want to see his face for a moment. His own father came all this way."

Tae-han chimed in, aggressive as ever. "Exactly! Don't make a scene over nothing. Even the director isn't barring us—who are you to play gatekeeper?!"

The hospital director cleared his throat, staring intently at the floor tile. Having already received explicit instructions from Yu-jung, he had no intention of inserting himself into the crossfire.

Yu-jung looked past Tae-han, studying the subtle twitches of anticipation masked beneath her family's somber expressions.

How thrilled they must be. The thorn in their side had finally been put down.

She gave a subtle nod to the attorney beside her. The lawyer stepped forward, smoothly opening a leather binder and presenting a document to the Chairman. A secretary took the file, handing it across to the patriarch.

As Chairman Kang skimmed the notarized clauses, his jaw locked tight.

Yu-jung spoke in a calm, melodic cadence. "That document grants me absolute power of attorney and full executive delegation over all of Kang Il-hyun’s assets, voting shares, and organizational commands in the event of his incapacitation or death."

Chairman Kang’s eyes narrowed into dangerous slits. "What is this supposed to mean?"

Yu-jung offered a brilliant, charming smile—one that carried an eerie, unmistakable resemblance to Il-hyun's own predatory smirk.

"I wonder. What could it possibly mean?"

Tae-han lost his temper completely. "Quit playing cute, Yu-jung! What the hell are you getting at?! Speak plainly!"

Yu-jung ignored him, keeping her dark eyes locked dead-center on Chairman Kang.

"It means that from this day forward... whoever wishes to murder Executive Director Kang will have to put a bullet through me first. Father."

The word Father dripped with raw, suffocating betrayal.

The muscle beneath Chairman Kang’s eye twitched violently. Beside him, Tae-han bellowed in outrage, "What are you implying?! Are you accusing us of hiring a hitman?!"

Chairman Kang raised a single hand, silencing the outburst.

He stared down his eldest daughter. Her lips were curved into a pleasant, filial smile, but the hatred burning in her eyes was naked and uncompromising. Unlike Il-hyun, who masked his venom beneath chaotic malice, Yu-jung had always kept her emotions tightly managed. Today, the armor was completely off.

Chairman Kang gave a slow, measured nod, handing the leather folder back as his hostile posture subsided into quiet, calculating defeat.

"We shall take our leave for today. Notify me the moment his condition stabilizes. You are not the only one who cares for that boy's life."

"Of course, Father."

Yu-jung bowed with immaculate, deferential grace.

Chairman Kang turned on his cane, leading his faction toward the elevators while the hospital director dabbed frantically at the cold sweat on his brow. The moment the elevator doors sealed shut, Yu-jung closed her eyes, her molars grinding together in silent fury.

Tae-soo stepped to her side. "You handled that exceptionally well, ma'am."

Yu-jung opened her eyes, letting out a long, shuddering breath before offering a bitter smile. When Il-hyun had first revealed the plot to her, she had been paralyzed by disbelief, followed by a blinding, white-hot rage. What kind of monstrous greed drives a father to put a contract on his own son's life just to cling to a corporate throne? It was beyond comprehension—and completely beyond forgiveness.

Dismissing the legal counsel, she followed Tae-soo into the sterile VIP suite.

She checked the digital telemetry monitors, her eyes drifting down to the thick, pristine bandages wrapping both of Il-hyun's legs. Restoring normal mobility would take months of intensive physical therapy.

"We should arrange a transfer to a private facility, shouldn't we?"

Tae-soo gave a firm nod. "I am currently securing a secure location. I will brief you the moment the transport is greenlit."

"Thank you, Chief Park. Having you by his side puts my mind at ease."

"I am merely executing my duty, ma'am."

"And the shooter?"

Tae-soo hesitated for a fraction of a second. Yu-jung was completely unaware that the assassin who pulled the trigger was Jang Yi-an—or rather, Lee Ja-kyeong. Il-hyun had laid the conspiracy bare to his sister, yet had deliberately withheld the sniper's identity. Tae-soo had no intention of breaking that silence.

"Our teams are tracking his movements."

A low, gravelly groan broke from the bed.

Il-hyun’s brow furrowed tightly as his head shifted against the pillow. Yu-jung rushed to the bedside while Tae-soo moved into position to monitor his vitals.

Dark lashes fluttered, heavy eyelids parting to reveal dilated, searching pupils.

Yu-jung leaned over him, her voice hushed. "Il-hyun? Can you hear me?"

Dark irises drifted across Yu-jung's face before sliding toward Tae-soo standing in the shadows behind her. Yu-jung asked if he was in pain, but received no answer. The hollow, vacant stare sent an icy dread plunging into her chest.

Reaching for a penlight to check his pupillary reflex, she froze.

A sharp, breathless chuckle broke from Il-hyun’s throat.

Yu-jung blinked in sheer bewilderment. Did he just... laugh? Did the fall cause a traumatic brain injury? The cranial CT scans had shown zero neurological trauma.

The chuckle deepened, rattling through Il-hyun’s broad chest in low, violent tremors until he was laughing out loud from the depths of his throat.

Terrified, Yu-jung turned a frantic look to the bodyguard. "What is wrong with him?! Why is he laughing like this?!"

Asking a security chief for a medical diagnosis was absurd, but having spent a decade shadowing Kang Il-hyun's darkest impulses, Tae-soo recognized the symptoms immediately.

"He is furious, ma'am."

Yu-jung’s eyes went wide. "This... is what he looks like when he's angry?"

Tae-soo kept his voice low, pitched strictly for her ears. "Yes. Immensely so."

In the vernacular of the streets, the man was absolutely, murderously pissed off. But Tae-soo spared her the vulgarity.

Yu-jung looked back down in horror. Il-hyun was still laughing, the display so unhinged that an outsider would think he was celebrating the birth of an heir rather than recovering from severed femoral arteries.

Slowly, the laughter died, evaporating from his features until his face set into an arctic, deadpan stillness.

Those pitch-black eyes burned with a terrifying, bloodthirsty brilliance.
Hrk—blegh!

Wang Ryun leaned over the rusted gunwale, dry-heaving violently into the churning foam.

The plan called for taking an old inshore fishing skiff out into the maritime corridor to rendezvous with an oceangoing smuggling freighter, but Ryun’s iron stomach had entirely surrendered to seasickness. Even heavy-duty scopolamine patches had failed him.

Once Ryun surrendered and staggered into the cramped lower cabin to collapse on a bunk, Jakyeong was left alone on the open deck, watching the dark, rolling swell.

The ocean was a pitch-black abyss, save for the rhythmic crash of whitecaps against the wooden hull.

Ten years ago, after Wang Han’s father had pulled a ten-year-old Jakyeong from the gutter and saved his life, they had fled Korea under the cover of night on a smuggling vessel just like this, cutting through the dark waters toward mainland China.

Jakyeong remembered lying awake on that rusty deck, paralyzed between the soaring relief of survival and the suffocating terror of the unknown. That was where he had met Wang Han and Wang Ryun—the only people in this wretched world who had ever functioned as family.

He reached into his leather jacket, drawing out his powered-down burner phone. Stored within its memory was Kang Il-hyun’s private number.

While the man lay immobilized in a hospital bed, Jakyeong needed to put thousands of miles between them. Living off the grid was second nature anyway; slipping into the shadows was what he did best.

Walking away without collecting the remaining balance stung, but combined with the advance, twelve billion won was a staggering fortune. He had taken half the money from both sides and delivered half of what each man wanted—neither the father nor the son had been shortchanged.

Whatever bloodbath unfolded between the Kang family from here on out was entirely their business. Whether they slaughtered each other or burned their empire to ash, he couldn't care less.

With a massive nest egg secured, he planned to scout private islands once the heat died down. Nothing too expansive—just a quiet, manageable plot of land. To make that dream work, he’d eventually need to find a sweet, ordinary girl to settle down with.

Where he’d drop anchor remained undecided, but one absolute truth was locked in stone: he was never stepping foot on Korean soil again.

Resting his forearms along the salt-crusted railing, he stared down into the churning water, letting the cold spray wash away the remnants of Seoul.

Lifting his gaze, a faint pinprick of light flickered across the distant horizon.

The beacon blinked in a rhythmic, repeating sequence: Short. Long. Short.

The smuggling freighter.

Jakyeong pushed himself off the railing, his boots steady against the rolling deck as the distant lights bore down through the dark.
